To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microenvironment of the CNS influences the morphology of the GINs and their AChR distribution, but has little effect on the distribution of Ca2+ channels.

the morphological redetermination and the distribution of synaptic receptors on the regenerating GIN neurites are determined by extrinsic cues, whereas the distribution of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels in the regenerating GINS is largely determined by intrinsic factors.
(1) The distribution of synaptic receptors on regenerating neurones is affected by extrinsic cues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms which control the redifferentiation process.
the role of the microenvironment in the recovery of neuronal function after injury.
the mechanisms underlying neuronal redifferentiation and regeneration in adult animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the environment of the CNS plays a role in the morphological rediffentiation of regenerating GAINs.
the environment provided by the connective is permissive for the growth of neurites, while the environment of the ganglion provides a permissive environment for the growth and branching of neurites.
the regenerating neurites respond to the local microenvironment, and that the response depends on the nature of the microenvironment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regrowth of severed neurones is a complex phenomenon.
the environment provided by the connective is not suitable for the morphological differentiation and the distribution of synaptic receptors of the regrowing axon.

(1) the pathway of regrowth is determined by the extrinsic cues, (2) the morphology of the regenerating neurones is determined by the microenvironment, (3) the distribution of ACHRs is determined by extrinsic cues, and (4) the distribution of Ca2+ channels seems to be determined by intrinsic factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
extrinsic cues govern morphological redifferentation and distribution of synaptic and other receptors.
the microenvironment of a regenerating neurone is important for morphological and functional redifferentiation.
the microenvironment plays a significant role in shaping the architecture of the regenerating neurones.
